d: In a landmark 9-6 ruling, the International Court of Justice has found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against its Rohingya minority. The court cited mass killings, widespread sexual violence and extreme violence against children, with evidence indicating that around 10,000 Rohingya were killed by Myanmar’s security forces. The 2017 military crackdown forced more than 730,000 Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh. Brought by The Gambia in 2019, the case marks the first time the World Court has found a state responsible for genocide. Hem Kaur Saroya tells you more on Vantage on Firstpost.
